questions.scenario: A massive fight breaks out in your society because someone parked their Swift Dzire in someone else's spot. How do you react?

options.text: Step in as the authoritative mediator, calm both uncles down, and restore order in the society.
Check the society's parking sticker on the car's windshield to see if the vehicle actually belongs to a resident.
Suggest clearing out the junk from the back alley to create a permanent community parking space for everyone.
Ask the society secretary to pull out the flat registry documents to prove who officially owns that exact parking slot.

questions.scenario: You are organizing a mega inter-school cricket tournament. What is your main responsibility?

options.text: Getting the official permissions from the principal, managing the chief guest, and overseeing the whole event.
Coordinating the school buses to ensure visiting teams arrive and depart exactly on schedule.
Ensuring the school groundsmen get proper refreshments and the junior kids get a chance to play too.
Keeping a strict diary of all the entry fees collected, equipment costs, and sponsor money.

questions.scenario: Your parents are finally agreeing to buy you a second-hand scooty for tuition. What is your focus?

options.text: Convincing them that you are responsible enough to handle the freedom and will follow all curfews.
Obsessively checking the RC book, pollution certificate (PUC), and ensuring the brakes are perfectly tuned.
Planning how you can help drop your younger sibling to their dance class or pick up groceries for Mummy.
Negotiating the exact resale value with the dealer and making sure the ownership transfer paperwork is spotless.

questions.scenario: A massive monsoon storm knocks down a huge tree, blocking the main road to your school. What's your move?

options.text: Take charge, tell everyone to stand back, and call the local helpline to get it cleared immediately.
Quickly stand at the intersection and guide the incoming school buses and autos to take a different route.
Gather the colony guards and helpers to chop the branches so the wood can be used by the local dhobi.
Check which house's boundary wall got crushed by the tree to figure out who has to pay for the damages.

questions.scenario: Your family is visiting a relative's village in tier-3 India for a summer wedding. What fascinates you?

options.text: How the village Sarpanch (head) commands so much respect and manages the entire village's affairs.
The local transport system—how tractors, shared autos, and buses navigate the muddy, narrow roads.
How government schemes are working there—like handpumps, solar streetlights, and the local Panchayat school.
The massive farm lands and how relatives keep track of which field belongs to which brother.

questions.scenario: Your class is setting up a food stall at the school Diwali Mela. What role do you naturally take?

options.text: The Stall Manager. You assign duties to everyone and handle the sudden rush of hungry students.
The Logistics Head. You figure out how to safely transport the heavy food pots from home to the school ground.
The Sourcing Head. You make sure you buy ingredients from local vendors and use eco-friendly patta plates.
The Cashier. You hold the cash box tightly, give exact change, and tally the profits at the end of the day.

questions.scenario: Your family is buying a new flat and sitting with the builder. What do you pay attention to?

options.text: How securely the society is managed—CCTV cameras, guards, and the rules of the Resident Welfare Association.
How wide the ramps to the basement parking are, and how far the society is from the nearest Metro station.
Whether the society has a proper rainwater harvesting system, solar panels, and a park for kids.
Looking at the heavy stamp-duty papers, floor plans, and registry documents the adults are signing.

questions.scenario: During a family road trip to a hill station, you hit a massive 2-hour traffic jam. What's your reaction?

options.text: Wonder why there is no police officer managing this chaos and wish you could step out to direct the crowd.
Analyze the bottleneck—is it a broken down truck, bad highway design, or an illegal toll booth?
Buy roasted bhutta (corn) from the local village kids selling on the highway to support them while waiting.
Mentally calculate how much extra petrol is being wasted and if the toll-plaza should refund the money.

questions.scenario: What is your favorite strategy when playing a board game like Monopoly / Business?

options.text: Making sure everyone follows the rules strictly, and acting as the Bank Manager to control the game.
Buying all the Railway Stations and transport hubs so everyone has to pay you when they move.
Upgrading spaces quickly so that the board actually looks developed with houses and hotels.
Hoarding property cards, keeping a hawk-eye on who lands on your space, and collecting rent ruthlessly.

questions.scenario: A new family moves into your neighborhood and they don't speak your local language well. How do you help?

options.text: Introduce yourself as the unofficial 'welcome committee' and help them settle into the society's routine.
Help them figure out the local bus routes, auto stands, and the quickest way to get to the main market.
Take them to the local community center or park so they can make friends and feel at home quickly.
Help them understand the local electricity bills, society maintenance charges, and address proofs.

State_Administrative_Officer_SDM.title: The City Commander (SDM / Sub-Divisional Magistrate)
State_Administrative_Officer_SDM.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader who loves taking charge. You handle crises well, make tough decisions, and keep everything in your city under control.
State_Administrative_Officer_SDM.day_in_the_life: Managing law and order in your district, overseeing state elections, coordinating during disasters, and making sure all government departments work together.
State_Administrative_Officer_SDM.alternative_match_text: If not civil services, your leadership skills would make you a great Event Manager, Operations Head, or Corporate CEO.
State_Administrative_Officer_SDM.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream. Degree: Any Graduation (BA/BSc/BCom/BTech). Next Steps: Clear the State Public Service Commission (State PSC) exams (like UPPSC, MPSC, RPSC, etc.).

Regional_Transport_Officer_RTO.title: The Transport Titan (Regional Transport Officer - RTO)
Regional_Transport_Officer_RTO.primary_match_text: You are fascinated by systems, vehicles, and movement. You love optimizing routes, ensuring safety, and enforcing rules on the road.
Regional_Transport_Officer_RTO.day_in_the_life: Issuing driving licenses, catching traffic rule breakers, inspecting vehicles for pollution and safety, and managing the public transport infrastructure of your region.
Regional_Transport_Officer_RTO.alternative_match_text: Your love for systems and movement makes you a perfect fit for Supply Chain Management, Logistics, or Automotive Engineering.
Regional_Transport_Officer_RTO.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Science preferred for engineering roles). Degree: Graduation (B.Tech in Automobile or Mechanical Engineering is a big bonus). Next Steps: Clear the State PSC exams.

Block_Development_Officer_BDO.title: The Grassroots Guardian (Block Development Officer - BDO)
Block_Development_Officer_BDO.primary_match_text: You are deeply connected to the ground reality. You want to uplift rural areas, help local communities, and build better infrastructure for those who need it most.
Block_Development_Officer_BDO.day_in_the_life: Visiting villages, checking if panchayat schools and wells are built properly, distributing government funds to farmers, and managing rural employment schemes (like MNREGA).
Block_Development_Officer_BDO.alternative_match_text: Your empathy and focus on development would make you a great NGO Director, Rural Management Expert, or Agricultural Officer.
Block_Development_Officer_BDO.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Humanities or Agriculture is great). Degree: BA in Rural Development, B.Sc Agriculture, or MSW. Next Steps: Clear the State PSC exams.

State_Revenue_Officer_Tehsildar.title: The Land Lord (Tehsildar / State Revenue Officer)
State_Revenue_Officer_Tehsildar.primary_match_text: You are highly detail-oriented and great with records, numbers, and documents. You believe in facts, clear ownership, and strict accounts.
State_Revenue_Officer_Tehsildar.day_in_the_life: Solving complex land disputes, overseeing property registries, collecting state land taxes, issuing caste/income certificates, and maintaining the vital records of the district.
State_Revenue_Officer_Tehsildar.alternative_match_text: Your eye for detail and documentation makes you a great fit for Real Estate Management, Chartered Accountancy (CA), or Corporate Law.
State_Revenue_Officer_Tehsildar.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Humanities. Degree: B.Com, BA, or LLB. Next Steps: Clear the State PSC exams or specific State Revenue Department examinations.
